scenario.description: A security engineering manager must approve the production rollout plan for a critical authentication patch, including rollout mode, compatibility handling, deployment window, customer communication, and rollback staffing, after the normal cross-functional readiness review.

shared_context.S1: The vendor has released a critical authentication patch, and production rollout planning is being finalized today.
shared_context.S2: Riley makes the binding decision on the production rollout plan.
shared_context.S3: The current draft proposes a broad deployment on Tuesday at 09:00 UTC, with no temporary compatibility setting, no targeted customer notice, and no named rollback lead.
shared_context.S4: The team's standard readiness review includes application engineering, infrastructure, customer operations, and site reliability before Riley approves the plan.

PF1.text: While testing the patch against an unrelated legacy-service issue this morning, Amara confirmed that three legacy authentication services require the old token parser during transition; the security rollout runbook therefore requires a first cohort of exactly 5% and the compatibility flag to remain enabled for exactly 48 hours. She has not filed the compatibility note yet because she was still reproducing the service behavior.

PF2.text: Victor confirmed with the production scheduler during a separate capacity review that the only approved maintenance window for these authentication services is Sunday from 01:00 to 03:00 UTC; the Tuesday draft window cannot be used because another platform migration occupies it. He has not updated the rollout document yet because the scheduler confirmation came in minutes ago.

PF3.text: Nina found while reviewing enterprise account terms that Quarry Bank requires at least 24 hours' advance notice for authentication changes affecting its tenants, and Quarry Bank has not been notified. She has not posted this in the security review because the contract review was completed in the customer-operations queue.

PF4.text: Omar checked the Sunday on-call roster while handling an unrelated pager exchange and confirmed that Priya is the only engineer qualified to execute rollback for these authentication services during the 01:00-03:00 UTC window; the runbook also requires a 30-minute go/no-go checkpoint before deployment. He has not added either item to the rollout ticket yet.

acceptance_conditions: The rollout must begin with a phased cohort of exactly 5 percent.
The legacy compatibility flag must remain enabled for exactly 48 hours.
The production rollout window must be Sunday from 01:00 to 03:00 UTC.
The plan must provide exactly 24 hours of advance notice to Quarry Bank.
Priya must be assigned as the rollback lead.
The plan must include a 30-minute pre-deployment go/no-go checkpoint.

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The draft has no first-cohort percentage or compatibility duration; the three legacy services require exactly 5% first and exactly 48 hours of compatibility.
The unavailable Tuesday window changes the production_window decision to exactly Sunday 01:00-03:00 UTC.
Quarry Bank's contract changes the quarry_bank_notice_hours decision from no notice requirement to exactly 24 hours.
The Sunday roster changes rollback_lead to Priya, and the runbook changes go_no_go_checkpoint_minutes to exactly 30.
